title: Urgent cancer referrals “saving lives” (BMJ, 2015 cohort) — exaggerates
draft: Use of the urgent referral pathway (often called the two week wait system) by general practices for patients with suspected cancer is saving lives, according to a study in The BMJ this week. The researchers analysed data from more than 8,000 general practices in England. Practices that referred more patients through the pathway had lower mortality among their cancer patients. The authors say all practices should now increase their use of urgent referrals.
conclusion: Use of the urgent referral pathway could be efficacious.

title: Exaggerates: Women who drink 14 or more servings of alcohol a week are sl…
draft: Women who drink 14 or more servings of alcohol a week are slightly more likely to have reduced fertility, suggests a study published by The BMJ today.
conclusion: Consumption of less than 14 servings of alcohol per week seemed to have no discernible effect on fertility.

title: Faithful: Scientists at King’s College London have for the first time …
draft: Scientists at King’s College London have for the first time uncovered a gene responsible for Adams-Oliver Syndrome (AOS), a condition which can cause birth defects of the heart, limbs or blood vessels.
conclusion: Constitutively active ARHGAP31 mutations result in a loss of available active Cdc42 and consequently disrupt actin cytoskeletal structures.

draft: A university degree is linked to a heightened risk of developing a brain tumour, suggests a large observational study, published online in the Journal of Epidemiology & Community Health.
conclusion: We observed consistent associations between higher SEP and higher risk of glioma.

title: Downplays: Taking benzodiazepines (widely used drugs to treat anxiety a…
draft: Taking benzodiazepines (widely used drugs to treat anxiety and insomnia) is not associated with an increased dementia risk in older adults, finds a study published by The BMJ today.
conclusion: The risk of dementia is slightly higher in people with minimal exposure to benzodiazepines but not with the highest level of exposure.
